surfaces.name: Web dashboard and headless server (localhost:23000, tmux agents)
AI Maestro iPhone app and Android beta (closed source)
AI Maestro Claude Code plugin, skills and CLI scripts

claims.answer: Browser dashboard (desktop, tablet and phone layouts, installable as a PWA) served by the host, a launcher command, and a separate iPhone app; macOS and Linux hosts, Windows via WSL2; no desktop-native app or editor extension; Android app is an email-invited beta.

desktop_os.answer: The server runs on macOS 12+ and Linux natively and on Windows only inside WSL2; it ships no native desktop app, only a Dock launcher that opens the dashboard.

mobile_apps.answer: An iPhone app is on the App Store (iOS 15.1+, 30 days free then $19.99 one-time per the vendor page); Android 7+ is an invite-only beta joined by emailing support. Neither app is in the public repositories.

browser.answer: Full dashboard at http://localhost:23000 with chat, terminal, board, matrix, attention and team pages; installable as a PWA over https or localhost.

mobile_browser.answer: Responsive phone layouts (MobileDashboard, MobileChatView) and Add to Home Screen; the README shows phone Matrix, home and board screens.

cli.answer: The installer adds an ai-maestro command (open, start, stop, status) and the plugin ships aimaestro-agent.sh, aimaestro-task.sh and AMP scripts.

editor_extensions.answer: Bounded search finds no VS Code or JetBrains extension; the Claude Code mods are plugins for that CLI, not editor extensions.

task_actions.answer: Create agents, send chat, steer through the terminal, answer approval and question cards, move cards and schedule work from the dashboard; review of code changes and resume of an old session beyond waking the agent are not separate flows.

notifications.answer: Push to the iPhone app through Expo (thin payload, 60 s cooldown); in-dashboard status, unread counts and Attention page; browser-level notifications are not documented.

cross_device_continuity.answer: Agents live in tmux on the host and the dashboard is stateless in the browser, so any device on the network or Tailscale sees the same agents; mesh peers show all hosts.

limitations: Windows only through WSL2.
Mobile apps are closed source and Android is an invite-only beta.
No editor extension.

claims.answer: Runs coding CLIs inside tmux: Claude Code, Codex CLI and Grok Build with chat, status and approval cards; Pi, Copilot CLI and OpenClaw with reduced support; any other terminal agent in the terminal tab. Also an embedded Claude Agent SDK chat path.

harnesses.answer: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Grok Build (first-class); Pi, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenClaw recognised; Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and others only as terminal programs; Aider deprecated.

model_providers.answer: Model choice is left to each CLI; the product only passes a model setting (--model) for some and documents Claude Code on Vertex AI and Pi with Gemini on Vertex.

custom_adapters.answer: Any terminal program can be set as an agent program and typed into; transcript readers (transcript-codex/grok/pi/copilot.mjs) are built-in modules rather than a plugin API.

session_integration.answer: Default path controls the CLI through tmux (paste-buffer and key presses) plus hooks and transcript reading; the Streaming tab embeds the Claude Agent SDK with canUseTool approvals.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: One dashboard and mesh can host Claude Code, Codex and Grok Build agents side by side that message each other over AMP.

limitations: Support depth differs per CLI.
No custom adapter interface; each reader is built into the server.

claims.answer: Uses each CLI's own login or API key; AI Maestro holds no model credentials. Subscription use follows whatever the CLI supports; no vendor credits.

agent_subscriptions.answer: Agents run the user's logged-in CLI (Grok needs SuperGrok/X Premium+, Copilot needs a Copilot subscription, Claude Code its own login); the README says to bring your own agent subscriptions.

api_accounts.answer: CLIs started with their own API keys work; Claude Code on Vertex AI and Pi on Vertex are documented with helper scripts.

vendor_credits.answer: No vendor credits, token sales or hosted tier exist ("no paid tier", "Is there a hosted version? Not yet").

local_models.answer: Pi can use a local OpenAI-compatible server and the repository tests used a fake local model, but local models are a property of the CLI, not an AI Maestro feature.

account_switching.answer: Bounded search of lib, services, docs and README finds no multi-account switching; each host uses whichever login its CLI holds.

vendor_account_requirement.answer: No AI Maestro account or login is required ("No account, no telemetry").

provider_restrictions.answer: Documents per-CLI login and subscription needs (Grok, Copilot) but no restrictions imposed by AI Maestro on third-party subscription use.

limitations: No account switching in AI Maestro itself; each host uses the login its CLI holds.

claims.answer: One-line installer (curl | bash) for macOS, Linux or WSL2 needing Node 24, tmux and about 4 GB RAM to build; first agent via wizard, CLI or by starting a tmux session; local directory, local git and GitHub repos all work; BYO VPS and AWS paths documented.

first_task_setup.answer: Install, open localhost:23000, create an agent with the guided wizard, wake it and chat; or run aimaestro-agent.sh create; any existing tmux session is auto-discovered.

no_git.answer: An agent is a working directory plus tmux session; git is not required to create or run one.

local_git_without_remote.answer: Repos are discovered by .git presence and read with git config; a remote origin is optional.

hosted_git.answer: A GitHub token can be passed to Docker and EC2 agents for push; the host environment otherwise uses the user's existing git credentials.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: README lists Node 24, tmux, RAM, WSL2 steps and Linux sizing; verify-installation.sh and the Doctor check readiness.

managed_cloud_setup.answer: No vendor-managed cloud exists ("Is there a hosted / cloud version? Not yet").

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: Documented Linux deployment guide, headless worker mode, remote-install.sh and the Terraform EC2 and ECS Fargate modules.

limitations: Manual steps for installing each CLI and logging in on every host.

claims.answer: Local REST API (no auth), WebSocket, shell scripts, signed webhooks and AMP API keys; no SDK; the product does not expose an MCP server for controlling the dashboard, only an MCP channel server for pushing messages into Claude Code.

cli.answer: aimaestro-agent.sh (create, rename, hibernate, wake, delete), aimaestro-task.sh, amp-* scripts and the ai-maestro launcher.

api.answer: Next.js REST routes under app/api for agents, chat, messages, tasks, teams, hosts, schedules, webhooks and a versioned AMP API at /api/v1.

sdk.answer: No client SDK is published in the inspected repositories.

mcp_server.answer: amp-channel-server.mjs is an MCP server that feeds inbox events into a running Claude Code session; no MCP server exposes agent control to other tools.

webhooks.answer: Webhook subscriptions with whsec_ signing secrets for agent and email events.

operations.answer: Create, inspect, chat/steer, hibernate, wake, delete, message and task operations exist in the API; stop is hibernate or tmux kill; code review is not an API operation.

authentication.answer: The dashboard API has no authentication by design; AMP /api/v1 uses hashed API keys with rotation and cross-host AID/Ed25519 signatures.

stability.answer: The dashboard API has no stability or deprecation policy in README, docs or SECURITY.md (bounded grep); the product is pre-1.0 (0.106.x) and only the AMP routes are namespaced /api/v1.

limitations: Unauthenticated dashboard API by design.
No SDK.

claims.answer: Agents are launched CLIs, so MCP and plugin support is inherited from them; AI Maestro adds a Claude Code plugin with 14 skills (Agent Skills standard), a plugin builder and a marketplace page, and an MCP channel server.

mcp_client.answer: MCP client features belong to the underlying CLI; AI Maestro only wires its own channel MCP server into Claude Code and offers Pi tool profiles that exclude mcp__* tools.

plugins.answer: Claude Code plugin (marketplace ai-maestro-plugins, 14 skills), plugin builder with 150+ personalities, and Claude Code mods for inbox and secrets.

custom_tools.answer: Skills and scripts add tools for agents; Pi gets a copied extension (amp_*); no generic custom-tool registry for all programs.

instructions_import.answer: Team-level markdown instructions and per-agent files; CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md handling is each CLI's; the installer writes a managed block into Pi AGENTS.md.

authentication.answer: Integration credentials go through aim-secret (vault) or each tool's own login.

permission_scope.answer: Per-program permission modes and a Pi messaging tool profile; skills have no separate scope model.

integration_owner.answer: Skills and scripts come from the AI Maestro plugin; MCP/tool wiring for other CLIs is owned by those CLIs; gateways are a separate repository.

limitations: Mostly inherited from each CLI.

claims.answer: Web app: Next.js/React with xterm.js terminal and a Node server (tmux via node-pty) plus a PWA manifest; no Electron or Tauri client; the iPhone and Android apps are closed and their stack is not published (vendor page calls the chat "native").

desktop_implementation.answer: No desktop client: the dashboard is a Next.js app with xterm.js/wterm terminals served by server.mjs; a Mac launcher only opens the browser.

mobile_implementation.answer: The iPhone and Android apps are not in the public repositories; the App Store listing and the vendor page do not state the framework (push uses Expo, which suggests but does not prove React Native).

hybrids.answer: Web UI plus PWA install; no hybrid wrapper in the repository.

implementation_evidence.answer: Pinned package.json and source cover the web app; mobile builds are closed.

limitations: Mobile client implementation not public.
claims.unknownReason: The mobile apps are closed source and their framework is not stated in first-party sources.

prompt_intake.answer: Prompts go through chat or typed instructions; schedules can issue prompts.

authoritative_tracker.answer: The JSON board files in the user's ~/.aimaestro are authoritative; no external tracker is linked.

stable_ids.answer: Cards have UUIDs (short prefix shown in instructions).

sync.answer: No external tracker sync exists in the inspected code.

supported_edits.answer: Edit subject, description, status, priority, assignee, owners, due, quadrant, waiting and blockers.

external_roundtrips.answer: Not applicable: nothing is synced to an external tracker.

acceptance_criteria.answer: No acceptance-criteria field on cards in the inspected types.

editors.answer: Card detail and board edit description and fields in the dashboard.

revisions.answer: Cards store comments but no edit history.

implementation_links.answer: Card origin links the agent, session, repo and thread that created it; commits trace back to sessions.

amendment.answer: A card can be edited while its agent works; instructions can be resent.

restart_persistence.answer: Boards are JSON files on disk that survive server restarts.

claims.answer: Flat cards with status, blockedBy dependencies (cycle-checked, readiness derived), kinds and quadrants; teams and projects group cards; no epics or arbitrary parent/child hierarchy and no dependency-gated dispatch.

epics.answer: No epic or parent field on cards; teams and projects are containers.

hierarchy.answer: Card hierarchy is not modelled; agents have a manager hierarchy and org chart instead.

blockers.answer: blockedBy lists of card IDs with a derived blocks list and isBlocked flag.

readiness.answer: isBlocked is computed from incomplete blockers and completing a card reports newly unblocked cards; there is no ready queue.

enforcement.answer: Blockers are shown, not enforced: no code stops an agent from starting a blocked card.

state_propagation.answer: Completion returns the unblocked cards but does not move them.

task_to_epic.answer: No epic concept to grow into.

identity_retention.answer: Not applicable: cards cannot grow into epics; a card keeps its UUID, comments and history across edits.

workflow_constraints.answer: No rigid workflow is required; any status can be set.

claims.answer: Per-agent working directory with CLI instructions, team-level markdown instructions, 14 skills, a skill marketplace and per-agent opt-in long-term memory (memory cards and entity graph with recall) plus code graph and generated docs.

instructions.answer: Team instructions field and each CLI's own instruction files; managed AGENTS.md block for Pi.

skills.answer: 14 skills in the Agent Skills format installed with the plugin plus a marketplace service.

project_docs.answer: Docs skill and DocumentationPanel index generated documentation of the agent codebase.

memory.answer: Nightly consolidation of conversations into memory cards and an entity graph, with recall injected on prompts, per agent opt-in.

scope.answer: Memory and code graph are indexed per agent and what it owns; team memory is not shared by default.

provenance.answer: Each memory statement is backed by the passages it came from.

correction.answer: A PATCH route edits a memory's content, category and context, and memories are rebuilt from sources by nightly consolidation.

deletion.answer: A DELETE route removes one memory by id and MemoryViewer has a per-memory delete button.

freshness.answer: Ended relations are marked and recurrence weights knowledge; nightly consolidation keeps it current.

takeover_continuity.answer: Memory and agent identity survive new sessions and agent transfer between hosts.

limitations: Memory is opt-in per agent and team memory is not shared by default.

claims.answer: Code graph (CozoDB, ts-morph, delta indexing), generated docs search, memory search and conversation search per agent; images through each CLI; no cross-repo knowledge connectors or review-time enforcement.

code_search.answer: graph-query and docs-search skills plus AgentSearch tab.

indexing.answer: Delta indexing of the codebase graph and transcripts (index-delta route).

external_knowledge.answer: Plugin personalities and gateways; no connector to external knowledge bases in core.

multimodal_inputs.answer: Agent uploads and AMP attachments exist; image reasoning depends on the CLI.

freshness.answer: Delta index updates and nightly memory runs.

access_scope.answer: Per-agent indexes keyed to the agent working directory.

api_retrieval.answer: REST routes for graph, docs, memory and search per agent.

citations.answer: Memory cards cite passages; graph answers list callers and dependencies.

create.answer: Create from dashboard, CLI and API.

discuss.answer: Comments with operator or agent authors.

label.answer: kind and org labels exist; no free-form labels.

assign.answer: Primary assignee plus up to 10 owners; project cards forward instructions to the assignee.

search.answer: The Matrix page filters cards by agent name or alias; no free-text search over card subjects or descriptions exists in the inspected components.

filter.answer: Matrix, Org and Attention views filter by quadrant, org, overdue and waiting.

archive.answer: Cards are completed or deleted; no archive state.

reopen.answer: Status can be moved back from completed.

project_epic_views.answer: Agent, team and project boards and an Org view; no epics.

idea_parking.answer: `aimaestro-task.sh park` saves an idea card (kind idea) off the board.

explicit_dispatch.answer: Assignment forwards a typed instruction to the assignee on project boards; own-board cards need the agent to read them.

task_session_separation.answer: Cards are separate from sessions and carry origin ids, but a card does not own sessions.

metadata.answer: Status, due, owners, origin, kind, quadrant, waiting, result, blockers, comments.

durable_states.answer: backlog, pending, in_progress, review, waiting, completed persisted with timestamps.

attribution.answer: Comments record operator or agent author; card field edits are not attributed.

permissions.answer: Agents can only delete cards on their own board; no per-user permissions.

concurrent_sessions.answer: Each agent is a tmux session; 80+ agents are described across hosts.

concurrent_tasks.answer: Each agent works on its own task concurrently.

quotas.answer: No agent-count quota found; AMP rate limit is 60 messages per minute.

observed_concurrency.answer: Vendor reports 80+ agents and a Linux memory sizing doc; this catalog did not run it.

status_visibility.answer: Working, Needs you, Ready, offline and hibernated states, unread counts and Attention page.

messages.answer: AMP signed messages with priority and types, delivered by Stop hook, channel or typing.

cross_harness.answer: Claude Code, Codex and Grok agents exchange AMP messages.

orchestration_owner.answer: Product-owned messaging and agent management skills; no hidden provider subagents.

live_progress.answer: Status and chat of any agent are visible; no parent-level child progress view.

retained_results.answer: Messages persist in the inbox files and transcripts.

schedules.answer: Cron expressions with timezone per schedule.

events.answer: Gateway messages and AMP messages wake agents; no repository event triggers.

recurring_tasks.answer: Morning triage, nightly checks and weekly reports are the documented use.

overlaps.answer: A run in flight is skipped.

stop.answer: Hibernate or delete agent; terminal Ctrl+C.

steer.answer: Chat or terminal at any time.

notifications.answer: Push to the iPhone app and in-dashboard Needs you; Slack/Discord gateways.

claims.answer: Agents run in tmux on your host, on mesh peers you own (including headless workers), in Docker, or on EC2/ECS Fargate in your own AWS account; no vendor cloud. tmux sessions keep running when the browser closes; the host must stay on.

local.answer: tmux on the host running the dashboard.

byo_remote.answer: Peer hosts over Tailscale or LAN, headless workers, EC2 and Fargate via Terraform.

self_hosted.answer: The whole product is self-hosted; each host runs its own server.

hybrid.answer: Mixed local, Docker and cloud agents appear in one dashboard.

provisioning.answer: Terraform modules provision EC2 and ECS from the dashboard or CLI.

payer.answer: The user pays their cloud provider and CLI subscriptions.

resources.answer: Docker agents default to 2 CPUs and 4g; Linux sizing guide for hosts.

region.answer: The user picks the AWS region through the aws_region Terraform variable (default us-east-1); there is no vendor region because there is no vendor cloud.

expiry.answer: EC2/ECS run until destroyed; Docker restart unless-stopped; no vendor lifetime.

client_disconnect.answer: tmux sessions persist after the dashboard or browser closes.

other_device_continuation.answer: Any browser or the iPhone app can reach the same host.

limitations: managed cloud: No vendor-operated cloud ("Not yet").
resources: Docker agents default to 2 CPUs and 4g; Linux sizing guide for hosts.
expiry: EC2/ECS run until destroyed; Docker restart unless-stopped; no vendor lifetime.

claims.answer: Default tmux agents run as the host user in their own working directory (separate clone), not worktrees; Docker agents get a hardened container with CPU and memory limits; EC2 gives a dedicated instance. No documented network or secret boundary for tmux agents.

checkout.answer: Each agent owns its working directory and clones what it owns.

branch.answer: Agents integrate through git branches by convention; no product branch management.

worktree.answer: The product deliberately does not use worktrees to isolate agents (README); agents may use them inside their clone.

container.answer: Docker agent runtime with --cap-drop=ALL, no-new-privileges, noexec tmpfs, --cpus and --memory.

vm.answer: EC2 agents run on dedicated instances through Terraform; no local VM isolation.

os_sandbox.answer: Only launch flags of supported CLIs (e.g. Codex sandbox mode); tmux agents are unsandboxed.

filesystem.answer: Container mounts /workspace plus listed mounts; tmux agents see the user home.

process.answer: Container PID namespace per agent; tmux agents share the user.

network.answer: Docker publishes a port and adds host.docker.internal; no network policy.

secrets.answer: aim-secret hides values from model context; file backend readable by the agent.

code_separation.answer: Separate clones per agent; shared folders produce a warning.

security_boundary.answer: SECURITY.md and Pi docs state tools restrictions are not a security boundary.
